title: ApostropheCMS apos create -- T1059.004 password-prompt shell command injection
author: WinstonRedGuard -- sigma plugin observed rules (derived from breach corpus)
description:
Vendor-disclosed detection for CVE-2026-42853 (GHSA-hcwq-x9fw-8cfq,
CVSS 6.5 MEDIUM), a self-reported advisory for `@apostrophecms/cli`
(up to and including 3.6.0), a Node.js CMS scaffolding tool.

`lib/commands/create.js:186` collects a password via an interactive
prompt and interpolates it directly into a shell command string passed
to `exec()` (a full-shell-interpreter call, not `execFile()`):
`exec(\`echo "${response.pw}" | ${createUserCommand}\`)`. The advisory's
own PoC password value -- `"; id > /tmp/apos_rce_proof.txt; echo "` --
breaks out of the intended `echo "<password>"` string and appends an
arbitrary shell command, with a captured proof-of-execution output of
`uid=1000(vboxuser) gid=1000(vboxuser) groups=1000(vboxuser),27(sudo),984(docker)`.
No patched version exists at authoring time (advisory lists "Patched
versions: None"); the advisory's own recommended fix is switching to
`execFile()`, which does not invoke a shell and therefore cannot
interpret injected metacharacters.

Detection logic flags the resulting host-level artifact: a shell
process spawned as a child of the `apos create` command whose command
line contains shell metacharacters immediately after an `echo` segment
-- the specific `echo "<value>" | <command>` construction the vulnerable
code builds is what makes a semicolon or backtick in the password value
become a new command rather than inert text.

Aggregated from 1 first-party vendor security advisory (apostrophecms,
via GHSA and NVD). No fix available at authoring time -- deployers
should avoid running `apos create` with untrusted password input until
a patch ships.
